featured_reviews.review_text: An emotionally charged holiday and hectic departure had triggered an excruciating migraine. I usually carry my meds with me but had checked them in my luggage and when we reached the terminal, I realized that I had no painkillers on me. I made my way towards the one pharmacy at the terminal and asked for a paracetamol. Open my wallet and realize that don't have any rupees in there except for a few coins. I offered to pay for just one/two pills with my coins or buy the 30 rupee packet by card but the card machine wasn't working. The good samaritan behind the counter saw my distress and generously offered the paracetamol to me. Unfortunately I didn't catch his name, but would like to thank him once again for his incredible gesture.  Not only did he save me from what would have been an arduous 15hr flight but he also restored my faith in humanity.
